references.text: The expression 'the steward of unrighteousness' (οἰκονόμον τῆς ἀδικίας) connects to Jesus' further teaching on unjust mammon in [ref:Luk 16:9-11|Luke 16:9-11], where he urges the disciples to use dishonest wealth wisely.

The verse belongs to the parable introduced in [ref:Luk 16:1|Luke 16:1], where the rich man's steward is accused of squandering his property. The Lord's praise of the steward in verse 8 is the climax of the parable.

Jesus uses a similar expression about wisdom in [ref:Matt 10:16|Matthew 10:16]: 'Be wise (φρόνιμοι) as serpents and innocent as doves.' The same root word for wisdom (φρόνιμος) is used here to describe the steward's conduct.

In the parable of the ten virgins in [ref:Matt 25:1-4|Matthew 25:1-4], a distinction is made between the wise (φρόνιμοι) and the foolish. The same adjective is used regarding the unjust steward's wisdom.

The contrast between 'the children of this world' and 'the children of light' (υἱοὶ τοῦ φωτός) has a parallel in [ref:Ef 5:8|Ephesians 5:8], where Paul writes: 'You were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Live as children of light.'
Paul refers to believers as 'children of light' (υἱοὶ φωτός) in [ref:1 Tess 5:5|1 Thessalonians 5:5], the same expression Jesus uses here to contrast them with the children of this world.
Jesus calls the disciples to believe in the light and become 'children of light' (υἱοὶ φωτός) in [ref:Joh 12:36|John 12:36], the same concept used in Luke 16:8 to describe believers.

In [ref:Matt 24:45-47|Matthew 24:45-47], Jesus praises the faithful and wise (φρόνιμος) steward who gives the household their food at the proper time. The theme of wise stewardship is shared with Luke 16:8.
In [ref:Ordsp 6:6-8|Proverbs 6:6-8], the ant is pointed out as an example of practical wisdom and future planning—a theme resembling the steward's wise, though dishonest, planning for the future.
In [ref:Luk 20:34|Luke 20:34], Jesus uses the expression 'the children of this age' (οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου), the same expression as in Luke 16:8 to describe worldly-minded people.
